title: Shopify says AI search is driving more traffic and sales, not replacing Google
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Shopify says AI isn’t cannibalizing search traffic the way it has for publishers. Instead, AI-driven traffic and orders to Shopify stores tripled year over year in Q2.
body:
Shopify recently reported robust second-quarter earnings, attributing a significant portion of its success to the burgeoning impact of AI search. Contrary to concerns in the publishing sector where AI summaries can reduce traffic, Shopify sees AI as a powerful complement to traditional search, not a replacement. The company highlighted a remarkable tripling of AI-driven traffic and orders to its stores year-over-year, emphasizing that this growth is additive, with conventional search traffic continuing to expand and remain a primary source of buyers. This indicates AI is expanding the overall market reach rather than simply reallocating existing search volume.

The effectiveness of AI search on Shopify stems from its sophisticated operational mechanism. Unlike conventional search engines that primarily rank products based on popularity and a limited set of keywords, AI agents leverage Shopify's extensive, structured product catalog. These agents perform multiple queries, delving deeper into the buyer's specific intent rather than just matching keywords. This nuanced approach allows for more precise product discovery, particularly benefiting the "long tail" of e-commerce – smaller merchants and niche products that might otherwise struggle for visibility against popular items in keyword-driven searches.

For developers and researchers, Shopify's experience offers a compelling real-world example of AI's transformative potential in e-commerce. It underscores the value of integrating AI with rich, structured data to facilitate intent-based matching, leading to enhanced discovery and sales. This success story provides a positive counterpoint to narratives of AI's disruptive impact, demonstrating how AI can drive substantial growth, expand market opportunities for diverse businesses, and ultimately create new value rather than merely optimizing existing processes or cannibalizing established channels.

title: Hark previews its browser use agent for completing tasks
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Hark claims that its browser use agent is faster and cheaper than competition.
body:
Hark, a startup that recently secured substantial Series A funding, has introduced "Hark Handoff," an innovative AI agent designed to efficiently automate tasks directly within a web browser. This agent aims to streamline user interactions across a multitude of websites, even those lacking dedicated APIs, such as major retail sites like Target and Walmart, or service platforms like OpenTable and LinkedIn. Handoff is built to execute a wide range of commands, from ordering essentials and booking travel to filing returns and conducting research, by intelligently navigating the digital landscape on behalf of the user.

The core of Handoff's functionality lies in its ability to interpret website structure and visual cues, enabling it to discern where to click buttons or input information. Hark differentiates its approach by claiming its model predicts the "next action"—a specific click or keyboard input—rather than merely predicting the next token, a common characteristic of large language models. Currently operating on a post-trained model, Hark plans to transition to pre-training later this year, a strategy intended to accelerate the refinement of its data pipelines, training infrastructure, and overall techniques.

This release holds significant implications for developers and researchers keen on advanced web automation. Hark positions Handoff as a competitive solution, asserting it outperforms rivals in speed and offers a more cost-effective alternative to high-end models like GPT 5.5 and Opus 4.8. As the field of computer-use agents continues to expand with contributions from tech giants and numerous startups, Hark's entry with Handoff underscores the growing potential for sophisticated, browser-based task automation. A waitlist is now open, with the platform slated for release by the end of summer.

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026’s Real World AI Stage features robots, automated factories, and extinct animals
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: On our new Real World AI stage, we’ll be focusing on the intersection between the digital and physical, and all the ways we’ll continue to see a blending of the two.
body:
## Expansion of AI Stages at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
The upcoming TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 event is set to feature an expanded AI presence, with not one, but two dedicated stages. The traditional AI Stage will continue to showcase the latest developments and innovations in the field, while the newly introduced Real World AI Stage will focus on the intersection of digital and physical technologies.

## Focus on Real-World Applications
The Real World AI Stage will explore the various ways in which autonomous hardware is being integrated into public spaces, homes, and even conservation efforts, such as bringing back extinct species. The stage will host speakers from prominent companies like Shield AI, Colossal Biosciences, and FieldAI, among others. The discussions will delve into the challenges and consequences of deploying AI systems in the physical world, where mistakes can have significant real-world implications.

## Implications for Developers and Researchers
The Real World AI Stage lineup will tackle tough questions, such as determining when an autonomous system is ready for safe deployment. This is a critical concern for developers and researchers working on hard tech projects, including autonomous vehicles, defense technologies, and industrial systems. By exploring these issues and showcasing the latest advancements, the Real World AI Stage aims to provide valuable insights and inspiration for attendees, who can join the event from October 13 to 15 at San Francisco's Moscone West.

title: Anthropic is hiring an AI chip design team
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Anthropic is building a team for designing its own custom AI chips. The Claude maker said it would co-design hardware and models to help its technology run faster and more efficien...
body:
Anthropic, the creator of the Claude AI model, has officially confirmed its strategic move into custom silicon development by establishing an in-house team dedicated to designing AI chips. This significant announcement signals the company's intent to optimize its AI infrastructure from the ground up. The primary objective is to co-design specialized hardware intrinsically linked with its AI models, aiming for substantial improvements in operational speed and overall efficiency.

This pivot towards proprietary chip design is a direct response to the escalating demand for Anthropic's AI services and the broader industry's scramble for high-performance AI computing resources. While Anthropic currently leverages partnerships with major providers like AWS, Google, Nvidia, and AMD, the company recognizes that long-term scalability and meeting future demand necessitate a more integrated and controlled hardware solution. Developing custom chips allows Anthropic to tailor its infrastructure precisely to the unique requirements of its large language models, moving beyond the limitations of general-purpose hardware.

For developers and researchers, Anthropic's venture into custom silicon underscores a critical trend among leading AI labs. Following in the footsteps of OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Meta, this move highlights a strategic imperative for major AI players to gain greater autonomy and efficiency in their computational backbone. This shift promises to unlock new frontiers in AI model performance and deployment, potentially leading to more powerful, energy-efficient, and specialized AI systems that can push the boundaries of what's currently possible.
